title: 東京のオフィス賃料が31年ぶり高値　人材獲得狙い移転、貸し手優位に
extracted_text:
東京でオフィス賃料の上昇が加速している。日本経済新聞社がまとめた2026年上期のオフィスビル賃貸料調査によると、東京の指数は31年ぶりの高値になった。人材獲得を急ぐ企業による優良ビルへの移転需要を背景に、貸し手優位の賃料相場が鮮明だ。

調査はオフィス仲介大手4社から賃貸料（募集ベース）で聞き取り、1985年2月を100として指数化した。東京の既存ビル（築後1年以上）の指数は183.64で前年同期比17.83ポイント（10.8%）高だった。既存ビルは賃貸市場の大半を占め、その値動きはオフィス需給の動向を反映しやすい。

25年下期の調査に続いて1年で1割の高い伸びを示した。リーマン・ショック前の高値を上回り、バブル期の高額賃料が終わり下落局面にあった1995年上期以来の高水準となった。

新型コロナウイルス禍に伴う在宅勤務からの出社回帰の流れへの対応や国内の構造的な人手不足を補うための人材獲得競争に向け、企業が広いオフィスを求めている。好立地で設備が整ったビルへの移転意欲が強い。入居しているビル内で空きが出るのを待っている企業も多いという。

一方、建設費の上昇を受けてビル建設がずれ込んでオフィス供給が抑えられやすい。貸し手側が物件コストを賃料に反映させる動きを強めている面もある。

市況をけん引するのは東京駅周辺だ。東京の既存ビルで最も賃料が高かったのは「丸の内〜大手町」地区で、中心値で前年同期比24.2%高の1坪（約3.3平方メートル）あたり5万6500円を付けている。大規模ビルが多く交通利便性も高いことなどから大企業の需要が根強い。

東京駅東側の「八重洲〜京橋〜日本橋」地区も前年同期比19.7%高の3万9500円。近年大規模ビルの供給が相次ぎ、企業の集積が進んでいる。 ホンダ や 中外製薬 などが今後完成する新ビルへの移転を決めている。

都心のオフィス不足感は強い。オフィス仲介大手の三鬼商事（東京・中央）によると、3月の都心5区（千代田、中央、港、新宿、渋谷）の空室率は2.22%と前年同月に比べ1.64ポイント低い。需給均衡の目安となる5%を下回る状況が20カ月続いている。

旺盛な需要や物価高を背景に、貸し手側は強気の賃料設定の姿勢を続ける。新規募集や契約更新の際に賃料を引き上げるほか、 三菱地所 や 三井不動産 、野村不動産といったビル大手では契約時の条件として、消費者物価指数（CPI）の変動によって賃料も上下する仕組みを導入する動きも広がっている。

ザイマックス総研（東京・港）の中山善夫社長はCPI連動を「物価上昇が当面続くとみて、相応の物件管理コストなどの増加分を即座に賃料に反映させる狙いがある」と指摘。「米国では一般的な考え方で、国内のオーナーもインフレ時代の標準になるかを見極めようとしている」とみる。

日経調査では、26年上期の東京の新築ビル（築後1年未満）の賃貸料指数も239.98と前年同期と比べて36.9ポイント（18.2%）高くなった。バブル期を終えた直後の1992年下期以来の水準にまで上昇した。

（森川美咲）

translated_text:
Office rent increases in Tokyo are accelerating. According to a survey of office building rental prices for the first half of 2026 compiled by the Nikkei Shimbun, Tokyo's index has reached a 31-year high. With companies urgently seeking to attract talent driving demand for relocations to higher-quality buildings, landlord-favorable rental market conditions have become pronounced.

The survey interviewed four major office brokerage firms about asking rents, with February 1985 set as 100. Tokyo's existing buildings (over one year old) posted an index of 183.64, up 17.83 points (10.8%) from the same period the previous year. Existing buildings account for the bulk of the rental market, and their price movements tend to accurately reflect office supply and demand trends.

Following the second half of 2025, the market showed a robust 10% growth over one year. This exceeds the high levels seen before the financial crisis, marking the highest since the first half of 1995 when the bubble-era high rents ended and the market entered a downturn.

Companies are seeking larger offices as they compete for talent to address both the return-to-office trend following the COVID-19 pandemic and the structural labor shortage in Japan. There is strong motivation to relocate to buildings in prime locations with solid amenities. Many companies are also waiting for space to become available in their current buildings.

Meanwhile, rising construction costs have delayed new building projects, limiting office supply. Landlords are increasingly passing their property costs onto rents.

The Tokyo Station area is leading the market. The highest rents in Tokyo's existing buildings were found in the Marunuchi-Otemachi district, with the median rent reaching 56,500 yen per tsubo (about 3.3 square meters), up 24.2% year-on-year. Strong demand from large companies persists due to the concentration of large-scale buildings and excellent transport accessibility.

The Yaesu-Kihin-Nihonbashi area on the east side of Tokyo also rose 19.7% year-on-year to 39,500 yen, with a series of large new buildings recently completed and corporate concentration advancing. Companies including Honda and Chugai Pharmaceutical have decided to relocate to new buildings currently under construction.

The shortage of office space in central Tokyo is acute. According to Mikane Shoji (Chuo-ku, Tokyo), the vacancy rate in the central five wards (Chiyoda, Chuo, Minato, Shinjuku, and Shibuya) was 2.22% in March, down 1.64 points from the same month last year. The situation has remained below the 5% equilibrium level for 20 consecutive months.

Amid strong demand and high inflation, landlords continue to take a firm stance on rent pricing. In addition to raising rents for new listings and lease renewals, major building operators including Mitsubishi Estate, Mitsui Fudosan, and Nomura Real Estate are increasingly adopting mechanisms that tie rent to Consumer Price Index fluctuations as a standard condition in contracts.

Zaimax Soken (Minato-ku, Tokyo) President Yoshio Nakayama commented on the CPI linkage, saying, "Given the expectation that inflation will continue for the foreseeable future, the aim is to immediately reflect increased property management costs and other expenses in rent. This is a common practice in the United States, and domestic property owners are watching to see if it becomes the standard in this inflationary era."

In the Nikkei survey, Tokyo's new building rental index (buildings less than one year old) for the first half of 2026 also reached 239.98, up 36.9 points (18.2%) year-on-year. This marks the highest level since the second half of 1992, immediately after the bubble era ended.

(Misaki Morikawa)
title_en: Tokyo Office Rents Hit 31-Year High as Companies Relocate to Attract Talent, Landlords Hold the Upper Hand
